text: I think the time to quit is when you can no longer see the vision and you can no longer really believe the vision. And then when that happens for a long period of time ...
speaker: Graham Weaver
context: Lenny asks Graham when someone should quit something, since some things are just not worth pursuing. Graham explains that the decision to quit should be based on whether you can still see and believe in your vision, rather than temporary setbacks or lack of excitement during difficult periods. He emphasizes that excitement isn't a reliable indicator during challenging times, but losing faith in the fundamental vision over an extended period is a clearer signal.
text_ko: 제 생각에는 그만둘 때는 더 이상 비전(vision)이 보이지 않고 그 비전을 진심으로 믿을 수 없을 때예요. 그리고 그런 상태가 오랫동안 계속된다면요...
text_zh: 我觉得该放弃的时候就是当你看不到愿景了，也不再真正相信这个愿景的时候。如果这种状态持续很长时间的话...
text_es: Yo creo que es momento de dejarlo cuando ya no logras ver hacia dónde vas y ya no crees realmente en esa visión. Y cuando eso pasa durante mucho tiempo...
key_sentence: Quit when you no longer believe in the vision during dark days.
original_text: I think the time to quit is when you can no longer see the vision and you can no longer really believe the vision. And then when that happens for a long period of time ... or maybe you're no longer even excited about the vision; somewhere in there, I think. The excited one, you have to be a little careful of, because in the dark days, exciting is not the word you're going to use.

vocabulary.definition: A vision is a clear and compelling idea of what an organization aspires to achieve in the future. It serves as a guiding star for strategic planning and decision-making.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a strong vision is essential for aligning team efforts and inspiring stakeholders, particularly in startups where direction and purpose are crucial for growth.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'vision' often conveys optimism and ambition, it can also imply a lack of practicality if not supported by actionable plans.

vocabulary.definition: To believe is to accept something as true or real, often without absolute proof. It involves a degree of trust or confidence in a concept or idea.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, belief in a company's vision, values, and potential is critical for motivating employees and attracting investors.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'believe' can imply a personal conviction that may not be universally shared, making it important to substantiate beliefs with evidence.

text: You start off and you're unconscious, and you're kind of going through the motions. And you may not even realize why you're doing what you're doing or even realize what you're doing.
speaker: Graham Weaver
context: Lenny asks Graham to explain his concept of 'autopilot mode' - the idea that most people go through life unconsciously without intentional direction. Graham describes how people can become unconscious and simply go through daily motions without realizing what they're doing or why. He uses the example of a typical workday routine to illustrate how people can live mechanically rather than intentionally.
text_ko: 처음엔 무의식적으로 시작해서 그냥 형식적으로 해요. 왜 그렇게 하는지, 심지어 지금 뭘 하고 있는지도 모를 때가 있어요.
text_zh: 刚开始的时候你其实是无意识的，就是在那儿走过场。你可能都不知道自己为什么要这么做，甚至都没意识到自己在做什么。
text_es: Al principio actúas sin darte cuenta, como en piloto automático. Y puede que ni siquiera entiendas por qué haces lo que haces, o incluso qué es lo que estás haciendo realmente.
key_sentence: you may not even realize why you're doing what you're doing or even realize what you're doing.
original_text: You start off and you're unconscious, and you're kind of going through the motions. And you may not even realize why you're doing what you're doing or even realize what you're doing. So for example, a typical person gets up, they have whatever their morning routine ... I get up out, work out, take a shower, drive into work, fight traffic, commute.

vocabulary.definition: Not aware of one's actions or surroundings; acting without conscious thought or intention.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, being unconscious can refer to employees or leaders who operate on autopilot, failing to engage with their work or make intentional decisions.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting a lack of awareness or mindfulness in professional settings.

vocabulary.definition: To become fully aware of something as a fact; to understand or grasp the significance of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, realizing a problem or opportunity is crucial for effective decision-making and strategic planning, as it prompts necessary actions.
vocabulary.nuance: This term can imply a moment of clarity or enlightenment, often used in contexts where awareness leads to significant change or action.

text: The formula, I think, for greatness is to be intentional, get in the path of the thing that you're most excited about, and then give yourself several decades to do it. And that's based on investing in 600 companies and building my own business.
speaker: Graham Weaver
context: Lenny mentions Graham's highly successful private equity fund performance and asks for comment. Graham responds by sharing what he believes is the fundamental formula for achieving greatness, based on his extensive experience investing in hundreds of companies and building his own business over decades. He emphasizes that this advice comes from real-world results, not just theoretical knowledge.
text_ko: 제가 생각하는 위대해지는 공식은 의도적으로 움직이고, 가장 가슴 뛰는 일의 길로 들어서서 그걸 해내기 위해 스스로에게 수십 년의 시간을 허락하는 거예요. 이 말은 제가 600여 개 회사에 투자하고 제 사업을 키워온 경험을 바탕으로 한 말이에요.
text_zh: 我觉得成就伟大的公式就是，要有明确的目标，然后去追求那个最让你兴奋的事情，再给自己几十年的时间去做这件事。这是我投资了600家公司、创建自己企业后得出的心得。
text_es: Creo que la fórmula para la grandeza es ser intencional, ponerte en el camino de lo que más te emociona, y luego darte varias décadas para hacerlo. Y esto lo digo después de invertir en 600 empresas y construir mi propio negocio.
key_sentence: Be intentional and get in the path of what excites you.

vocabulary.definition: Deliberate and purposeful; done with a specific intention or goal in mind.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, being intentional refers to making strategic decisions that align with long-term objectives, rather than acting on impulse or without clear direction.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'intentional' conveys a sense of thoughtfulness, it can imply a lack of flexibility if overemphasized.

vocabulary.definition: The act of allocating resources, usually money, in order to generate an income or profit.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup ecosystem, investing often refers to funding new ventures with the expectation of future returns, either through equity or debt.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'investing' typically implies a financial commitment, it can also refer to investing time or effort in projects or relationships.

vocabulary.definition: The quality of being outstanding or extremely good; a high level of achievement or excellence.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, greatness can refer to a company's reputation, innovation, or leadership in its industry, often used to inspire teams and set ambitious goals.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'greatness' carries a positive connotation but can be subjective, as what constitutes greatness may vary across different contexts and cultures.

text: Pick anything. You want a better body? Okay, you're going to need to go to the gym. When you go to the gym the first few times, it's going to not be that fun. The first move is negative.
speaker: Graham Weaver
context: Lenny references Graham's quote about 'everything you want is on the other side of worse first' and asks him to explain it. Graham illustrates this concept by explaining that any worthwhile change requires initial discomfort or difficulty. He uses the example of getting in shape to show how the first steps toward improvement are often unpleasant, and if you optimize for short-term comfort, you'll never make meaningful progress.
text_ko: 아무거나 골라도 돼요. 몸을 더 좋게 만들고 싶어요? 그러려면 헬스장에 가야 해요. 헬스장에 처음 몇 번 가보면 별로 재미없을 거예요. 첫 시도는 항상 가장 힘들고 기분이 안 좋을 수 있어요.
text_zh: 随便举个例子吧。想要更好的身材？那你就得去健身房。刚开始去健身房的那几次，肯定不会很爽。第一步总是痛苦的。
text_es: Elige lo que sea. ¿Quieres ponerte en forma? Perfecto, vas a tener que ir al gimnasio. Las primeras veces que vayas al gimnasio no te va a gustar nada. El primer paso siempre es duro.
key_sentence: The first move is negative when optimizing for tomorrow.
original_text: Pick anything. You want a better body? Okay, you're going to need to go to the gym. When you go to the gym the first few times, it's going to not be that fun. The first move is negative. If I'm optimizing for tomorrow and I just want to have a great day tomorrow, I'm going to stay exactly where I am.

vocabulary.definition: Expressing denial, disagreement, or a lack of something; often associated with adverse outcomes or conditions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, a negative report or feedback can indicate poor performance, risks, or challenges that need to be addressed.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can carry a heavy connotation, suggesting not just a lack of positivity but also potential harm or setbacks.

vocabulary.definition: The initial action taken in a sequence of events; often the first step in a strategy or plan.
vocabulary.businessContext: In competitive business environments, the 'first move' can refer to the advantage gained by being the first to enter a market or implement a new strategy.
vocabulary.nuance: The phrase can imply both opportunity and risk, as the first move can set the tone for subsequent actions and responses from competitors.

text: And I have this unbelievable statement. I didn't write it. Dan and Chip Heath wrote it in their book, Switch, which is 'Scale your bright spots.
speaker: Graham Weaver
context: Graham is explaining when to quit versus when to persist with something difficult. He shares a key principle from the book 'Switch' about focusing on what's working rather than what's failing. He uses his own company Alpine as an example, explaining that even during the first difficult 10 years, they could always identify small successes or 'bright spots' that they could build upon and scale.
text_ko: 정말 믿기 힘든 말이 있어요. 제가 쓴 말은 아니고요. 댄과 칩 히스가 쓴 책 스위치(Switch)에 나오는 표현인데요, '잘 되고 있는 부분들(bright spots)을 키우세요.'
text_zh: 我有个特别棒的说法，不是我说的，是丹和奇普·希思在他们《转变》这本书里写的：'把你的亮点放大'。
text_es: Y tengo esta frase increíble. No es mía. Dan y Chip Heath la escribieron en su libro Switch, que dice: "Multiplica lo que ya te está funcionando bien" (scale your bright spots).
original_text: And I have this unbelievable statement. I didn't write it. Dan and Chip Heath wrote it in their book, Switch, which is 'Scale your bright spots. Find what's working and do more of that.' And as you start to progress, for me, for example, at Alpine, almost all the time, we always had at least a small glimmer of a bright spot.

vocabulary.definition: To increase in size, number, or capacity, often in a systematic manner.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, scaling refers to the ability of a company to grow its operations and revenue without being hampered by its structure or available resources when facing increased production demands.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'scale' often implies growth, it can also suggest the need for efficiency and sustainability in that growth.

vocabulary.definition: Positive aspects or successful elements within a larger context, often used to identify areas of strength.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, identifying 'bright spots' can help organizations focus on successful strategies or practices that can be replicated or scaled to improve overall performance.
vocabulary.nuance: The term suggests optimism and potential, often used in contrast to challenges or weaknesses that may be present.

text: The thing that we probably believe to be true that not that many people agree with us on is that the management team is really where we think all the alpha comes from.
speaker: Graham Weaver
context: Lenny asks Graham what his private equity firm looks for in companies that others might not focus on. Graham explains Alpine's distinctive investment philosophy - that exceptional management teams are the primary source of returns (alpha). He clarifies that while you can't choose a completely failing industry, having world-class leadership is more important than finding the perfect market opportunity.
text_ko: 우리가 아마 사실이라고 믿지만 많은 사람이 동의하지 않는 게 하나 있다면, 바로 모든 초과수익(alpha)이 결국 경영진의 역량에서 나온다고 보는 거예요.
text_zh: 我们坚信但可能很多人不认同的一点是，管理团队才是真正产生超额回报(alpha)的地方。
text_es: Lo que nosotros creemos que es verdad, pero en lo que no mucha gente está de acuerdo con nosotros, es que el equipo directivo es realmente de donde creemos que viene todo el alfa.
key_sentence: The management team is where all the alpha comes from.
original_text: The thing that we probably believe to be true that not that many people agree with us on is that the management team is really where we think all the alpha comes from. You can't get the industry wrong, because if you hire the best management team in the world to run a typewriter business, you're going to lose money.

vocabulary.definition: A group of individuals responsible for overseeing and making decisions regarding the operations and strategy of an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, the management team plays a crucial role in guiding the company's direction, making strategic decisions, and ensuring that the organization meets its goals.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often implies a collaborative effort among leaders, and its effectiveness can significantly impact the company's success.

vocabulary.definition: A measure of an investment's performance relative to a benchmark, often used to indicate the excess return generated by an investment strategy.
vocabulary.businessContext: In finance, alpha is a key metric for evaluating the effectiveness of fund managers and investment strategies, with a positive alpha indicating outperformance.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can also refer to a broader concept of leadership or dominance in business contexts, but is most commonly associated with investment performance.
